goal: Add and end-to-end verify safe repo-local RunPod GPU browser testing infrastructure for Codex and Claude Code.
observations: Worktree was clean at task start on codex/wave1-build-experiment.
The project already uses Node >=20, Playwright 1.56.1 under tools/, and deterministic SwiftShader browser helpers; hardware-GPU runs must use a separate launch path.
Existing reports explicitly defer native visual captures and Tier-H performance evidence because the local container uses SwiftShader.
The original RunPod key was rejected with HTTP 401. After owner rotation, doctor, inventory, Pod lifecycle, and cleanup requests authenticated successfully.

RunPod's live inventory can return qualitative stock with availableGpuCounts omitted; the selector now safely accepts non-None qualitative stock and lets Pod creation make the final capacity decision.

Two deliberately cancelled diagnosis runs proved SIGINT cleanup and deletion. They showed that the generic template exposes port 22 but does not start sshd; the runner now supplies a repo-owned sshd entrypoint and both current and legacy public-key environment names.

Live run 20260813-105749Z-9265 used Community RTX A2000 at $0.12/hour, completed in 125.3 seconds, rendered the game through NVIDIA Vulkan hardware WebGL 2, retrieved PNG/WebM/log/JSON artifacts, and confirmed Pod qcq80dxsmtlwwp deleted by a subsequent 404.

Local self-tests pass 7/7: allowlist/price/capacity selection, idempotent deletion, ambiguous-create no-retry including POST server errors, orphan cleanup scope, dirty-worktree snapshot fidelity, and ephemeral SSH key generation.
A fail-closed one-minute CLI run recorded the original authentication failure, created no Pod, and correctly recorded cleanup as unnecessary.
The generic RunPod template is sufficient without modification; a purpose-built image is an optional startup-speed optimization only.
next_step: Use npm run gpu:doctor, npm run gpu:list, then npm run gpu:test; use gpu:cleanup after any abruptly lost agent session.
